prose.text: {{common-actions-in-console}} {{two-discovery-endpoints}} {{provider-prefers-all-endpoint}} {{python-has-only-old-endpoint}} Between v3.8.45 and the pin the Go name `AllAvailableActions` moved onto the new endpoint {{all-available-actions-reassigned}}. prose.text: {{python-docstring-action-vocabulary}} {{docstring-misfiled-entries}} The MCP tool forwards its inputs to the SDK {{mcp-actions-tool-forwards}}, which the workflow skill does not reflect {{divergence:mcp-representative-app-probing}}. checks.do: Which action strings are valid for the selected applications and rule type, read from the discovery endpoint rather than written by hand.
For an exact answer about the actions one application offers, ask for one application at a time.
Whether a template set on a CAC rule is shown to users, which needs a test rather than a reading of the rule form.

console-actions.statement: A Cloud App Control rule's console action is Allow, Caution, Block, Conditional or Isolate; Isolate requires Zero Trust Browser.

quotes: Choose to allow the users to access the selected applications.
Choose to display an EUN that cautions users before allowing them access to the selected applications.
Choose to block the users from accessing the selected applications.
Choose to conditionally allow the users to access the selected applications.
Choose to isolate all the traffic that matches the cloud app control rule through a remote browser.
This action is available only if Zero Trust Browser is enabled for your organization.

actions-is-a-list.statement: In the API the rule's `actions` field is a list of strings, not a single value, so one rule can carry several action strings. The Go SDK model, the Python model's request format and the provider's `actions` set all use a list.

expect.description: Action taken when traffic matches rule.

action-string-shape.statement: Each action string is a prefix naming the verdict followed by application and operation tokens, for example ALLOW_AI_ML_CHAT, DENY_AI_ML_UPLOAD, BLOCK_FILE_SHARE_DOWNLOAD, CAUTION_AI_ML_WEB_USE and ISOLATE_AI_ML_WEB_USE. The provider recognises the prefixes ALLOW, DENY, BLOCK, CAUTION, ISOLATE and ESC (conditional access).

isolate-not-mixed.statement: ISOLATE actions cannot be combined with other actions in one rule, and a rule using them needs a Cloud Browser Isolation profile (`cbiProfile`).

quotes: ISOLATE actions require cbi_profile configuration and cannot be mixed with other actions.
Note: This parameter is required for the ISOLATE action and is not applicable to other actions.

common-actions-in-console.statement: When several applications with granular controls are selected in one category, the console shows only the actions common to all of them.

quotes: If more than one cloud application with granular controls is selected for a category, then only the actions that are common among the selected applications are displayed.

two-discovery-endpoints.statement: The Go SDK has two action-discovery calls, both taking a rule type and a request of `cloudApps` and `type` and returning a flat list of strings: `AvailableActions` (POST /{rule_type}/availableActions) and `AllAvailableActions` (POST /{rule_type}/allAvailableActions). The release notes describe the second as retrieving all available actions for each application type.

provider-prefers-all-endpoint.statement: The provider's rule-actions data source calls AllAvailableActions first and falls back to AvailableActions only when the error is a typed response with HTTP 404 or 405. Any other failure (400, 401, 403, 5xx, or an error that is not a typed response) is returned to Terraform without a fallback. It sets available_actions to the returned list in the order received (after the optional JMESPath search), splits ISOLATE_ actions from the rest, and applies the optional prefix filter after the search.

python-has-only-old-endpoint.statement: The Python SDK exposes only the older availableActions call, and its request body carries `cloudApps` without a `type` key. It has no counterpart for allAvailableActions.
python-has-only-old-endpoint.conditions: Absence claim from reading zscaler/zia/cloudappcontrol.py at the pin: the only action-discovery method is list_available_actions, which posts to /webApplicationRules/{rule_type}/availableActions.

no-custom-eun.statement: The deployment guide states that Cloud App Control policies do not support custom End User Notifications.

quotes: Cloud App Control policies do not support custom End User Notifications (EUNs).

rule-notification-fields.statement: A rule form still carries notification fields: a Browser Notification Template (when the action is Caution or Block), an End User Notification Show/Hide choice (only when a granular action is blocked, shown by default) and a Notification Message for the Zscaler Client Connector-based EUN. The rule model has `eunEnabled`, `eunTemplateId` and `browserEunTemplateId`.
rule-notification-fields.conditions: Corrected on recapture (2026-10-18): previously "A rule form still carries notification fields: a Browser Notification Template (when the action is Caution or Block), an End User Notification Show/Hide choice (only when a granular action is blocked, shown by default) and a Custom Message for Zscaler Client Connector. The rule model has `eunEnabled`, `eunTemplateId` and `browserEunTemplateId`." The recaptured page labels the field Notification Message, not Custom Message.

quotes: This field appears when the application access is set to either Caution or Block.
This field appears when the granular action is blocked for the selected applications.
This field is set to Show by default.
Notification Message: Select a notification message that you want to show as the Zscaler Client Connector-based EUN.

all-available-actions-reassigned.statement: At Go SDK v3.8.45 the exported `AllAvailableActions` posted to /{rule_type}/availableActions. At the pin the same exported name posts to /{rule_type}/allAvailableActions and `AvailableActions` holds the older /availableActions path, so a caller compiled against the earlier name selects a different endpoint after upgrading.

automate-capture-availableactions-only.statement: The captured Automate OpenAPI document describes one action-discovery operation, POST /webApplicationRules/{rule_type}/availableActions ("Fetches the granular actions supported for the applications"), and lists no allAvailableActions path.

expect.description: Fetches the granular actions supported for the applications.

python-docstring-action-vocabulary.statement: The per-category action vocabulary (for example IT_SERVICES, LEGAL, SALES_AND_MARKETING) is enumerated in the Python `add_rule` docstring; the Go model types `Actions` as a plain string list with no equivalent enumeration. The docstring lists `CAUTION_LEGAL_USE` under IT_SERVICES and `DENY_DNS_OVER_HTTPS_USE` under LEGAL.

docstring-misfiled-entries.statement: The docstring entries `CAUTION_LEGAL_USE` under IT_SERVICES and `DENY_DNS_OVER_HTTPS_USE` under LEGAL look misfiled.
docstring-misfiled-entries.conditions: Inferred from naming: the other entries in each list carry their category's own token, and these two carry another category's token or name another feature; no source says they are misplaced.

mcp-actions-tool-forwards.statement: The MCP list-actions tool forwards `rule_type` and the optional `cloud_apps` list to the Python SDK `list_available_actions` and returns what comes back; it does no category-level probing.

quotes: if err: raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to list CAC actions for {args.rule_type}: {err}")

mcp-skill-per-tuple-validation.statement: The MCP create workflow skill says the create endpoint validates each `(rule_type, app, action)` tuple, that a multi-app create is frequently rejected with `INVALID_INPUT_ARGUMENT: "Invalid action provided for selected applications"`, that the first incompatible pair fails the entire create, and that one rule per app is the safe pattern. The executable create tool does no such validation: it assembles the payload and calls the SDK `add_rule`.

The first incompatible (app, action) pair fails the entire create.
in practice ZIA frequently rejects multi-app rules with `INVALID_INPUT_ARGUMENT: "Invalid action provided for selected applications"`
so the only safe pattern is to split.

all-vs-available-differs.title: How allAvailableActions results differ from availableActions
all-vs-available-differs.blocks: knowing which actions an older client or fallback path omits
all-vs-available-differs.detail: The release note says the new endpoint retrieves all available actions for each application type, and the provider guide says the fallback 'may omit some newer actions'. Neither source defines which actions differ, and static source cannot show it.

quotes: which may omit some newer actions

multi-app-aggregation.title: What the action endpoints return for several applications
multi-app-aggregation.blocks: trusting an action list built from more than one cloud app
multi-app-aggregation.detail: The generated provider guide says the API returns only actions supported by all of the listed applications. The provider code and Go wrappers do not define the aggregation (union, intersection or other), whether list order is meaningful, or whether a result is valid for each individual app; the guide's intersection wording is documentation, not evidence of API behavior. Query one application at a time when the answer matters. The console's common-actions behavior is documented separately (claim common-actions-in-console).

quotes: When multiple applications are specified, the API automatically returns only actions supported by ALL applications.

custom-eun-meaning.title: What 'no custom EUNs' excludes when rules carry template fields
custom-eun-meaning.blocks: telling an operator whether a notification template set on a CAC rule takes effect
custom-eun-meaning.detail: The deployment guide says CAC does not support custom EUNs, yet the rule form and model have browser notification template, EUN and custom message fields. No source says what users see when a template is set. The earlier statement that blocked users see the default notification is not stated by any registered source.

per-tuple-validation-contract.title: Whether the create call validates each (rule type, app, action) tuple and rejects a mixed multi-app rule as a whole
per-tuple-validation-contract.blocks: creating one Cloud App Control rule for several apps in a single call
per-tuple-validation-contract.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the whole-create rejection, the INVALID_INPUT_ARGUMENT message and the one-rule-per-app pattern come from an MCP workflow skill, not from either SDK or the executable tool. Static code cannot settle it; a live create with a mixed-validity app list would. Tracked in the legacy ledger as zia-53.

quotes: The first incompatible (app, action) pair fails the entire create.

representative-app-actions.title: Whether action discovery needs a category representative app, and whether allAvailableActions removes the need
representative-app-actions.blocks: trusting an action list obtained for a single app as the category vocabulary
representative-app-actions.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the MCP workflow generalizes that discovery may be surfaced through a category representative app. That guidance predates the Go allAvailableActions path, and static code does not show that the new endpoint removes the need for it. Comparing both endpoints with single-app and multi-app requests would settle it. Tracked with the atomic-validation gap as zia-53.

quotes: not every app in a category is a "representative" the API surfaces actions for

mcp-representative-app-probing.summary: Whether the MCP action-discovery tool matches the workflow skill's description of it

quotes: the app the API actually returned actions for (may differ from `resolved_app` because not every app in a category is a "representative" the API surfaces actions for — the tool walks the category until it finds one that does)

positions.says: The create workflow skill calls `zia_list_cloud_app_control_actions(cloud_app=...)` and describes a result with `category`, `resolved_app` and `actions_surfaced_via`; it says the tool walks the category until it finds a representative app.

The executable tool takes `cloud_apps` (a list), forwards `rule_type` and `cloud_apps` straight to the SDK, and returns the plain list of actions; it has no category walk and no `category`, `resolved_app` or `actions_surfaced_via` field.

mcp-representative-app-probing.impact: An agent following the skill expects a diagnostic field and a probing step the tool does not implement; the skill describes behavior that the pinned code lacks.
